What are your slow cooker recipes?

Grape Jelly Meatballs. Now I know you're thinking, "That's the worst sounding shit ever" - Until you try it. Very easy to make, you add the meatballs, BBQ sauce (Sweet Baby Rays), and either the same or 1/2 grape Jelly compared to the BBQ sauce you added. I usually do about 32 ounces of meatballs, 18 ounces of BBQ, and 9 ounces of grape jelly. Cook on high 3 hours, and you have some of the best meatballs you will ever taste in your entire life.
I've made similar with grape jelly and yellow mustard. It was what I was going to post, but ya stole ma thunder, @Samsquamch!
Shredded Mexican chicken: 1 can of salsa + 2 chicken breasts. Shred with fork after a few hours. Cook 4-6 hours. Put on tacos of your desired crunchiness, or make nachos, or just eat.
Sauerkraut & kielbasa. Add chopped dill, black pepper, & bacon to preference. It's a heavy meal, no doubt.

Teriyaki chicken. 2lbs chicken, 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/4tsp ginger, 1/4tsp garlic powder, 1/2 Tbsp ketchup, 1-2 Tbsp sesame seed optional. Cook 6-7hrs on low or 3-4hrs on high. Toss in stir fry vegetables for last hour and serve over rice. One of my favorites.

As for cooking, exploring spicy foods was a big motivator to learning to cook. Not much spicy on this site of the country (mostly lazy heat without the flavor). That or recreating long lost favorites from restaurants.
I just made something very similar but I also put in hoisin sauce, oyster sauce, onion powder and red pepper flakes.
This pulled pork recipe is simple and pretty good: http://www.porkbeinspired.com/recipes/perfect-pulled-pork/

Carnitas. I just use recipes I find online. Not always super flavorful but they will last you a few days. That and frozen meatballs and that thick teriyaki sauce (la choy I think). Use the cooker to heat them through and eat them on those kings Hawaiian sweet rolls. I'll usually make some white rice with them too.

Slow cooked roast...

Go buy a cheap roast (pork or beef...pork is usually cheaper), a package of baby carrots, an onion, a packet of brown gravy, a packet of Italian dressing, a packet of ranch dressing and a package of brown sugar (You can use the liquids of Italian/Ranch, too and/or make your own gravy)

Sear the roast in a skillet for a few seconds on each side.

Put it in your slow cooker, add in the peeled onion (whole), baby carrots and thick-chopped potatoes.

Add in the whole packet of gravy, 1/2 packet of Italian, 1/2 packet of Ranch (or dollops of each) and 2~3 tablespoons of brown sugar.

Cover with water until barely covered. Cook 6~8 hours. When it falls apart, eat it. Eat all of it.
I've had this and it is delicious!!!!

Remeber that Cambell's has slow cooker sauce. But just using one bottle of Masterpiece Original BBQ sauce can do the trick for those that want a stronger favor.

This message brought to you by Brand Power. /s But in all seriousness the Cambell's sauce is decent so if you don't have ingrediants on hand for a sauce it does the trick. It is a bit under flavored. I've had some trouble firgureing out exactly what to augment it with while keeping the favor but I'll get it one of these days.

Venison rump roast. Soak the roast in whole milk overnight, then rinse. Place in slow cooker on medium heat with red russet potatoes, a whole sweet onion, two cloves of garlic, medallion sliced carrots, a whole can of Buffalo Rock Ginger Ale, two bay leaves, a tea spoon of salt, and two teaspoons of basil and rosemary.

Cook all day. Turn it on when you leave in the morning, come back at the end of the day, and enjoy.

There's this stuff called menudo. Few chopped up pig's feet, few pounds of tripe (menudo regular is less expensive) chopped into 1 in. squares, a whole onion in chunks, a whole bulb of garlic separated into cloves (no need to peel), some peppers, some dried oregano, cook for 6 or 12 or 15 hours. Some people add hominy. Some people start by boiling the tripe 1 minute, throwing out the water, and then adding the tripe to the pot. It takes a lot of salt at the end. Serve with tortillas. Throw some fresh chopped onions, many lime squeezes, and a sprinkling of dried oregano and dried chile into the bowl. My God it's good.

Slow cooker chicken with 40 cloves of garlic. I know what you're thinking, too much garlic. But the sauce is buttery and amazing, and the cooked garlic melts on your tongue (just like the chicken!). Added bonus is that the place where you live will smell amazing, seriously, bring a woman over when it's done because panties will drop. Unless you're looking for a guy, same effect though.

4 chicken breasts, or a whole chicken, whatever...about 3-4 lbs anyway.

1 large jar of green pepperoncini.

If the pepperoncini jar doesn't have enough liquid to cover the chicken, add water until covered.

Cook while at work. When done, you can pull it and make spicy chicken salad, or make a sandwich or whatever.

Add can of mushroom soup Add onion, carrot, celery, and mushroom Add garlic, salt, and pepper Add chicken breasts Cook all day covered on Low
